examples.brief: A LinkedIn post on when hempcrete is worth its cost premium, for architects with an embodied-carbon target.
examples.post_text:
Hempcrete locks away roughly 110 kg of CO₂ per cubic meter, and it keeps getting stronger as it carbonates. That carbon stays in the wall for the life of the building.

Here are the trade-offs we lead with, every time:

It isn't structural. Hempcrete is an insulating infill, paired with a timber or steel frame.
Cure time is longer than block, so it has to be sequenced into the program early.
The envelope carries a cost premium of 5 to 12%.

What you get back is a documented service life of 50 to 100 years, and breathable walls that buffer humidity instead of trapping it.

On the Larkfield mixed-use block, hempcrete and reclaimed cladding cut embodied carbon 38% against the baseline spec. The material helped. Being in the room at RIBA Stage 2 helped more.

Specify it early, and specify it for what it is.

#EmbodiedCarbon #Hempcrete #BioBasedMaterials #SustainableConstruction

examples.brief: A statement card on why every material claim needs a number attached.

fields.headline: A material that can't show its numbers doesn't belong in the spec.
fields.body: We ask for embodied carbon in kgCO₂e/m², a U-value, and an end-of-life pathway. "Sustainable" without a number is just a feeling.
fields.cta: Ask us where our numbers stop

examples.brief: A LinkedIn post and a quote card on the mycelium acoustic panels in the Halden studio fit-out.
examples.post_text:
Reverberation time in the Halden studio dropped from 1.4s to 0.6s after we installed 400 mycelium acoustic panels.

Each panel grows into the exact shape of its mold in about a week. Then we heat-set it to stop the growth. Indoors, it is warrantied for 15 years, and at the end of its life it is home-compostable.

The note the architect sent back is the one we keep coming back to: "first acoustic product I haven't had to hide."

Bio-based doesn't have to mean something you cover up. It can be the thing you put on show.

#Mycelium #BioBasedMaterials #BiophilicDesign

document.title: Bio-based envelopes, costed honestly
document.lede: A low-carbon envelope can cost more up front. Here is where the premium comes from, what it buys, and when a hybrid spec is the better answer.

sections.heading: What the premium is
sections.body: Bio-based materials often carry a 5 to 15% premium at the envelope; for hempcrete it runs 5 to 12%. Sometimes it disappears once thermal mass cuts plant size. Sometimes it doesn't, and we will say so.
bullets: Hempcrete is an insulating infill, paired with a timber or steel frame
Cure time is longer than block, so it is sequenced into the program early
Reclaimed timber is specified to availability, not the other way around

sections.heading: What it returns
sections.body: The return is carbon you can report and fabric that lasts. A credibly low-carbon building also carries asset value, a planning advantage, and an ESG claim that survives due diligence.
bullets: Roughly 110 kg of CO₂ sequestered per cubic meter of hempcrete
A documented service life of 50 to 100 years for hempcrete walls
Breathable walls that avoid interstitial condensation

sections.heading: Where the big wins come from
sections.body: On the Larkfield mixed-use block, hempcrete and reclaimed cladding cut embodied carbon 38% against the baseline spec. It worked because we were in the room at RIBA Stage 2, before the structural grid was locked.
bullets: We model cost both ways and show you the honest number
We publish cradle-to-gate and cradle-to-grave figures for every product
Where the premium doesn't pay back, we recommend a hybrid spec

document.footer: Verdure Materials: evidence, candor, and early involvement.
